entries.title: Structure shows the author's sub-sections
entries.body: Structure can go one level deeper: where an author has split a section into numbered or headed sub-sections, each gets its own row with a title and a short summary. The rows follow the author's own sub-headings, not the AI's guess, and a section whose headings do not line up is left as it was. This applies to articles whose Structure is made or re-run from today; existing ones keep the outline they have.

entries.title: Citation lists hold up to 300 works
entries.body: In Sources, the list of works an article cites asks the AI for every work the piece cites, passage by passage, and holds up to 300 rather than 80. Before, it kept only the 80 the piece leaned on most, so long papers' lists stopped short. Existing lists stay as they are until re-run.
